title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: What’s Behind a Recent Spike in Early Social Security Claims?
summary: Experts point to well-publicized turmoil at the government agency last year as a potential spark.

title: Ahead of Thanksgiving, Readers Show Grace and Grit
summary: KFF Health News gives readers a chance to comment on a recent batch of stories.

title: Meet the Teen Who Called a Hospital Home
summary: A young survivor of gun violence lived on the third floor of a St. Louis children’s hospital, moving through the halls in a wheelchair, on and off for over three years. He said it became his home when he had nowhere safe to go.

title: Trump Administration OKs Native Traditional Healing for Two States’ Medicaid Programs
summary: The administration’s expansion of traditional healing for Native Americans comes as it shrinks Medicaid in other ways, including through restrictions that will affect access to care for an estimated 7.5 million people.

title: ‘A Hard Time’ as Federal Cuts Hobble Efforts To Stop Overdoses From Tainted Drugs
summary: Harm reduction proponents say testing street drugs prevents overdoses by allowing people to make more informed decisions about what they’re using, but the Trump administration contends that it promotes drug use.

title: Moving to a New State? Your Healthcare Might Get More Complicated
summary: New apartment, new friends, new … healthcare hurdles? Medical matters might not be at the top of your list when moving to a new state. But planning ahead will help you get the health insurance, doctors, and healthcare access you need.

title: These Governors-Elect Campaigned on Expanding Medicaid. It Won’t Be Easy.
summary: A handful of states that haven’t fully expanded Medicaid just elected Democratic candidates for governor who campaigned on broadening access to the government health insurance program for low-income people. But doing so won’t be so simple given recent changes to Medicaid, including looming work requirements.

title: States Offer Perks To Attract Healthcare Workers to Rural Areas — With a Catch
summary: States are using some of the $50 billion from the Rural Health Transformation Program to provide incentives to healthcare providers to practice in rural America. But the money comes with strings attached: a five-year service commitment.

title: The US Long Treated Measles as a Preventable Tragedy. Under Trump, It’s Roared Back.
summary: All but vanquished a quarter century ago, measles has taken root again in the U.S. Compared with prior administrations, President Donald Trump’s second term has been marred by misinformation and actions that stifle public health.
